events.title: Magellan Reaches the Philippines
events.description: Ferdinand Magellan's Spanish expedition sighted the island of Samar in the Philippines during its attempt to circumnavigate the globe, landing the next day on the nearby island of Homonhon.
events.significance: This marked the first European arrival in the Philippines and was a key milestone in the first circumnavigation of the Earth, leading to centuries of Spanish colonial presence in the archipelago.

events.title: United States Military Academy Established
events.description: President Thomas Jefferson signed legislation establishing the United States Military Academy at West Point, New York.
events.significance: West Point became the nation's first military college and trained generations of American military and engineering leaders, including Ulysses S. Grant and Robert E. Lee.

events.title: The Scarlet Letter Published
events.description: Nathaniel Hawthorne's novel The Scarlet Letter was first published in Boston, telling the story of Hester Prynne in Puritan New England.
events.significance: The novel became a cornerstone of American literature and a lasting exploration of sin, guilt, and social judgment.

events.title: My Lai Massacre
events.description: U.S. Army soldiers killed hundreds of unarmed Vietnamese civilians in the villages of My Lai and My Khe during the Vietnam War.
events.significance: Public revelation of the massacre in 1969 intensified opposition to the Vietnam War and prompted major debate about military conduct and accountability.

events.title: Former Italian Prime Minister Aldo Moro Kidnapped
events.description: Aldo Moro, former Prime Minister of Italy and leader of the Christian Democracy party, was kidnapped by the Red Brigades in Rome, and his five bodyguards were killed.
events.significance: Moro was held for 54 days and killed in May 1978, an event that became a defining moment of Italy's 'Years of Lead' and shaped the country's political landscape and counterterrorism efforts.
